root_cause.text: In `ext4_fc_replay_inode()` in the ext4 fast-commit recovery path, error exits bypassed `brelse(iloc.bh)`, leaking the buffer-head reference obtained by `ext4_get_fc_inode_loc()` and leaving the function’s error handling inconsistent.
root_cause.evidence: The patch notes that `ext4_get_fc_inode_loc()` “holds a reference to `iloc.bh` that must be released via `brelse()`,” and shows multiple `goto out;` paths after `ext4_handle_dirty_metadata()`, `sync_dirty_buffer()`, `ext4_mark_inode_used()`, and `ext4_iget()` failures being changed to `goto out_brelse;`, with a new `out_brelse:` label calling `brelse(iloc.bh)` before `out:`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix ext4 fast-commit inode replay error handling to always run buffer cleanup before returning failure.
intent_record.what: The error paths in ext4_fc_replay_inode() were changed to jump to out_brelse instead of out after ext4_handle_dirty_metadata(), sync_dirty_buffer(), and ext4_mark_inode_used() fail. In the ext4_iget() failure case, the function no longer returns -EFSCORRUPTED directly; instead it sets inode to NULL, assigns ret = -EFSCORRUPTED, and jumps to out_brelse.
intent_record.how: This change ensures the buffer head cleanup path is executed on all these failure exits, preventing resource leakage and keeping the function’s cleanup behavior consistent even when inode replay or lookup fails.

intent_record.intent_summary: Return the real replay error status instead of always succeeding.
intent_record.what: A new label `out_brelse:` was inserted immediately before `brelse(iloc.bh);`, and the function’s final return statement was changed from `return 0;` to `return ret;`.
intent_record.how: The function now propagates the actual status from `ext4_handle_dirty_metadata()` instead of always reporting success, so callers can detect replay/metadata write failures; the added label preserves the existing cleanup path structure.

bic_trace_step.reason: Yes, the snippet contains the exact vulnerable replay function and the problematic error exits. In `static int ext4_fc_replay_inode(...)`, the code obtains a buffer head via `ret = ext4_get_fc_inode_loc(sb, ino, &iloc);` and then uses `iloc.bh`. On the success path it eventually does `brelse(iloc.bh);`, but the early error path does `if (ret) goto out;` and the `out:` label only does `iput(inode);` and `blkdev_issue_flush(...)` — there is no `brelse(iloc.bh)` there. Likewise, if `ext4_iget(...)` fails after writing the inode, it returns `-EFSCORRUPTED` directly, also bypassing any buffer-head release. This matches the root cause: error exits in `ext4_fc_replay_inode()` bypass `brelse(iloc.bh)`, leaking the buffer-head reference. The fix is not present in this commit body because no error-path cleanup for `iloc.bh` appears at the `out:` label or before the direct return.

bic_trace_step.reason: Yes, the snippet contains the relevant replay function and its error exits. In `static int ext4_fc_replay_inode(struct super_block *sb, struct ext4_fc_tl *tl)`, the function obtains a buffer head via `ret = ext4_get_fc_inode_loc(sb, ino, &iloc);` and then uses `iloc.bh` later. The vulnerable pattern is visible because several failure paths jump directly to `out` before any `brelse(iloc.bh)` is issued: `if (ret) goto out;`, `if (ret) goto out;` after `ext4_handle_dirty_metadata`, `if (ret) goto out;` after `sync_dirty_buffer`, and `if (ret) goto out;` after `ext4_mark_inode_used`. At `out:` the code only does `iput(inode);` and optionally flushes, but never releases `iloc.bh`. The only `brelse(iloc.bh)` in the function appears on the success path near the end, right before `out:`. Therefore the buffer-head reference leak on error exits is present, and the fix is not yet in this version.
